patterns.description: Migrate from ObservableObject protocol to @Observable macro by removing @Published property wrappers. The macro generates compile-time source code that automatically handles property observation without requiring property wrappers. SwiftUI provides backward compatibility so StateObject and EnvironmentObject work with @Observable types during incremental adoption.

Point-Free's Composable Architecture uses @ObservableState macro on Reducer State structs to support modern SwiftUI observation patterns while maintaining backward compatibility with legacy ViewStore and WithViewStore patterns. This allows mixing old and new observation mechanisms during incremental migration.

When using property wrappers like @Shared alongside @Observable, annotate with @ObservationIgnored to avoid macro conflicts. Swift macros don't play nicely with other property wrappers, so explicit ignorance prevents compilation errors while @Shared handles its own observation.

Swift's @preconcurrency attribute marks concurrency isolation as conditional, allowing public APIs to adopt Swift 6 features without breaking existing clients. Applies to MainActor, imports, and protocols - Swift 5 clients see no isolation requirements while Swift 6 clients get full enforcement.

TCA demonstrates mixing legacy features (ViewStore/WithViewStore) with modern @ObservableState patterns. While functional, this can cause view bodies to re-compute more often than necessary due to differing observation mechanisms - acceptable temporary trade-off for phased adoption.

Use MainActor.assumeIsolated and MainActor.run to bridge migrated and unmigrated code safely at runtime. This enables calling MainActor-isolated code from non-isolated contexts during gradual migration, with runtime crash protection if assumptions are violated.

Point-Free's Swift Sharing library demonstrates deriving smaller shared state pieces from larger values using property access syntax. Child features work with only needed data while changes propagate back to parent, enabling clean state management across complex dependency graphs.

Swift's error() and warning() macros generate diagnostic messages at compile time. Useful for staged migrations where certain code patterns should trigger warnings during transition periods before becoming errors in final target state.

TCA maintains Store's ObservableObject conformance even after adding @ObservableState macro support. This doesn't affect actual observability but ensures backward compatibility with code expecting ObservableObject interface during migration period.

insights: Apple officially supports incremental @Observable adoption with backward compatibility guarantees - StateObject and EnvironmentObject continue working with @Observable types, enabling gradual migration without breaking existing View code

Property wrapper conflicts are the primary source of @Observable migration compilation errors - @ObservationIgnored is required when combining @Observable with other property wrappers like @Shared, @StateObject, or custom wrappers

TCA's migration to 1.7+ demonstrates real-world complexity of large-scale @Observable adoption - they maintained ViewStore compatibility while introducing @ObservableState, accepting some performance overhead during transition

Swift 6 concurrency migration patterns directly apply to @Observable transitions - @preconcurrency, dynamic isolation bridging, and staged API changes provide proven patterns for maintaining build stability during architecture transitions
Compile-time macro diagnostics (Swift.error/warning) provide migration guardrails - can emit contextual errors for unmigrated code patterns to guide developers toward target architecture

State derivation patterns from Swift Sharing enable complex dependency graph management - larger parent models can vend scoped child state that automatically propagates changes, reducing coordination complexity during multi-feature development
ObservationIgnored macro is specifically designed for @Shared persistence strategies that need to coexist with @Observable - fileStorage, appStorage, and inMemory persistence all require this pattern

MainActor.assumeIsolated enables calling migrated @Observable code from legacy ObservableObject contexts during incremental transition - runtime assertion rather than compile-time enforcement provides flexibility for complex migration scenarios
gaps: No documented pattern for managing 20+ simultaneous compilation errors across multiple in-flight features on a broken base branch - current guidance focuses on incremental adoption rather than rescue operations
Limited guidance on coordinating @Observable migration across teams working on parallel feature branches - Apple and Point-Free documentation assumes single-team incremental adoption
No specific pattern for temporarily disabling observation during base branch stabilization - unclear whether partial @Observable adoption can be safely reverted without cascading compilation failures
Missing best practices for CI/CD pipeline handling of @Observable migration - no documented approaches for maintaining buildable main branch while feature branches contain partial migration states

Insufficient guidance on ObservableObject protocol method compatibility during migration - unclear how custom combine publishers or objectWillChange implementations translate to @Observable equivalents
